hints.title: Positive Elements vs Non-Positive
hints.text: Since arbitrary elements can be deleted before selecting a contiguous segment, consider how deleting non-positive numbers or duplicate values helps maximize the remaining sum.

hints.title: All Non-Positive Edge Case
hints.text: If every number in the array is zero or negative, the result must be a single non-empty element, which corresponds to the maximum element.

hints.title: Sum of Distinct Positives
hints.text: If there is at least one positive integer, delete all negative numbers, zeros, and redundant duplicate positive numbers so all distinct positive numbers become adjacent.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of elements in nums
complexity.notes: Single pass collects unique positive values and checks maximum element.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating all possible subsets or subarray deletion combinations takes exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: A collection of unique positive numbers uses linear auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Identify that arbitrary deletions allow consolidating all distinct positive numbers into a single subarray.
